subject: health
unitTitle: Substance Misuse Trends, Refusal Skills, and Support Pathways
title: Guided practice: impaired driving and passenger decisions
essentialQuestion: How do I hold a decision when the pressure is quiet, repeated, and from someone close?
materials: guardian-approved local and national support resource list
keyPoints: Impairment affects reaction, coordination, and judgment; a transportation plan must cover both driving and riding with a driver who may be impaired.
Risk reduction combines accurate information, an advance prevention or refusal plan, a safe exit, and trained help; one protective step should not be treated as a guarantee.
For impaired driving and passenger decisions, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build a support-pathway map for three fictional situations of escalating seriousness, naming the trusted adult, the service, and the point at which emergency help is called.
studentTask: Analyze a supplied fictional situation about impaired driving and passenger decisions. Make a three-part safety plan—risk cue, refusal or prevention step, and adult or emergency support—and explain why the plan is safer than relying on one warning or one refusal line.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in impaired driving and passenger decisions; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the impaired driving and passenger decisions task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: The map may be drawn, listed, dictated, or completed on a supplied template. Reading load may be reduced with summarized resource descriptions.
extensionChallenge: Apply impaired driving and passenger decisions under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of impaired driving and passenger decisions in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.

contentProvenance.objective: Explain impaired driving and passenger decisions accurately using current, reliable health information rather than assumption or anecdote.
